On this page

Connecting a Repo ​

A project is a repo Saidi knows about. Registering one gives you a project agent scoped to that checkout, and a memory file that carries the repo's policy and its durable facts.

Register the project ​

Ask PRIME in chat, or use the tools directly:

ToolWhat it does
discover_projectsScans your configured scan roots for git repos
sync_projectsReconciles the registry with what is on disk
add_projectRegisters one repo explicitly (name + path)
list_projectsShows the registry
update_project / remove_projectEdit or drop an entry

The registry name you choose is what PRIME uses as the delegation target and as the assignee on checklist tasks — keep it short and unambiguous.

Set the project's policy ​

Each project's policy lives in the frontmatter of its memory file, memory/projects/<name>.md:

markdown
---
branch: new        # new | current
approval: confirm  # confirm | auto
verify: npm test   # optional: shell command run after a work delegation commits
---

# my-app

## Purpose
...
KeyValuesDefault
branchnew cuts a saidi/* branch and opens a PR; current commits on the checked-out branchnew
approvalconfirm asks before any write; auto proceeds without a promptconfirm
verifyA shell command run after a work delegation commits. Pass/fail is reported mechanicallynone

There is no global default that silently applies — an unset, missing, or invalid value falls back to the built-in safe policy (new + confirm), unless you have changed the operator fallback in Settings → System. Parsing is lenient: unknown keys, inline # comments, and quotes are ignored.

verify: is the cheapest trust you will ever buy

With verify: npm test set, "done" stops being the agent's claim and becomes an exit code in the change note. Set it on every repo that has a test command.

Fill in the memory file ​

Below the frontmatter, the memory file is free-form markdown that gets injected into the project agent's prompt. Worth recording:

  • Purpose — what the repo is, in one line.
  • Layout & scripts — top-level dirs, and the dev / build / test commands.
  • Deploy steps — the exact procedure, if there is one.
  • Notes / gotchas — required env vars, ports, things that break.

Memory is not committed to your repo. It lives in Saidi under memory/projects/, so your repo stays clean and the knowledge follows the operator.

First delegation ​

Start with an ask — a read-only investigation — before you let anything write:

Ask my-app: what does the auth middleware do, and where is the session validated?

An ask delegation runs the project agent with a read-only tool set (Read, Grep, Glob). When you are satisfied it understands the repo, promote to work.
